text.tspan: You have a candidate rhodopsin
and want its peak wavelength in nm
Is there a training sequence
of the same length within
5% Hamming distance?
Nearest training sequence looked best here:
MAE 6.60 nm vs a constant's 16.16 nm on these 5 rows.
Descriptive only, n = 5: a signpost,
not a supported recommendation
179 of 184 held-out rows land here:
no close training sequence
Hit a desired band, 540 to 560 nm
Composition + fixed ridge put 9 of 10
in band against 0.31 expected at random.
Post-hoc interval 0.33 to 1.00
Estimate the wavelength itself
Best MAE 24.36 nm vs a constant's 24.60 nm:
-0.24 nm, 95% CI -0.45 to -0.05, too small to act on.
Post-hoc 90% intervals need about ±38 nm
and cover only 77% to 84% of test rows
Maximise red shift
None beat chance at the extremes: composition missed all 7 rows
at or above 580 nm, though its top-10 mean beat random
(553.5 vs 534.4 nm, post-hoc). ESM-2's 587 nm hit is within
chance: a random top 10 holds a row >= 580 nm with P = 0.33
ESM-2 35M frozen residue mean + fixed alpha-10 ridge
was worse than a constant on this split:
8M: +4.30 nm, CI includes zero, no supported difference
One split, one adaptation: not a verdict on ESM-2
or on fine-tuned models, which were untested
